      28                 :             : /**
      29                 :             :  * @file synchronized.h
      30                 :             :  * @brief Small helper providing serialized access to an object.
      31                 :             :  *
      32                 :             :  * @section what What is Synchronized?
      33                 :             :  * Synchronized<T, Lockable> wraps an object of type T together with a Lockable
      34                 :             :  * (std::mutex by default) and provides RAII-based, mutex-protected access
      35                 :             :  * to that object. All reads and writes are expected to go through lock()
      36                 :             :  * or WithLock(), making the relationship between the object and its lock
      37                 :             :  * explicit and harder to misuse.
      38                 :             :  *
      39                 :             :  * @section member_types Member Types
      40                 :             :  * - value_type: The type T of the synchronized object.
      41                 :             :  * - pointer: LockedPtr<T, std::unique_lock<Lockable>>
      42                 :             :  * - const_pointer: LockedPtr<const T, std::unique_lock<Lockable>>
      43                 :             :  *
      44                 :             :  * @section how How does it work?
      45                 :             :  * - Internally stores:
      46                 :             :  *     - mutable Lockable mut;
      47                 :             :  *     - T obj;
      48                 :             :  * - lock():
      49                 :             :  *     - Acquires mut via std::unique_lock.
      50                 :             :  *     - Returns a pointer (or a const_pointer for const Synchronized)
      51                 :             :  *       with the lock held which is released when the returned pointer goes out of scope.
      52                 :             :  * - WithLock(Func&& f):
      53                 :             :  *     - Acquires the lock.
      54                 :             :  *     - Invokes the callable f(pointer) or f(const_pointer) with the lock held.
      55                 :             :  *     - The lock is released when f returns (or exits due to an exception).
      56                 :             :  *
      57                 :             :  * @section usage Usage Example
      58                 :             :  * Basic example:
      59                 :             :  * @code
      60                 :             :  * using score::concurrency::Synchronized;
      61                 :             :  *
      62                 :             :  * Synchronized<Sender> sender(local_endpoint, remote_endpoint);
      63                 :             :  *
      64                 :             :  * // Modify
      65                 :             :  * bool success = sender.WithLock([message](pointer sp) {
      66                 :             :  *     return sp->send(message);
      67                 :             :  * });
      68                 :             :  *
      69                 :             :  * // Read
      70                 :             :  * auto total_messages = sender.WithLock([](const_pointer sp) {
      71                 :             :  *     return sp->stats.num_successful_messages + sp->stats.num_failed_messages;
      72                 :             :  * });
      73                 :             :  * @endcode
      74                 :             :  *
      75                 :             :  * For a longer critical section:
      76                 :             :  * @code
      77                 :             :  * Synchronized<std::vector<dtc_status>> dtc_statuses;
      78                 :             :  *
      79                 :             :  * if (auto new_dtcs = receive_dtcs(); !new_dtcs.empty()) {
      80                 :             :  *     auto dtcs = dtc_statuses.lock();    // mutex locked
      81                 :             :  *     dtcs->reserve(dtcs->size() + new_dtcs.size());
      82                 :             :  *     dtcs->insert(dtcs->end(), new_dtcs.begin(), new_dtcs.end());
      83                 :             :  * } // dtcs goes out of scope, mutex unlocked
      84                 :             :  * @endcode
      85                 :             :  *
      86                 :             :  * @note
      87                 :             :  * - The default Lockable is std::mutex, which is non-recursive.
      88                 :             :  *   Locking the same mutex multiple times from the same thread has
      89                 :             :  *   undefined behaviour
      90                 :             :  *   (see https://en.cppreference.com/w/cpp/thread/mutex/lock).
      91                 :             :  * - Therefore, calling lock() / WithLock() re-entrantly on the same
      92                 :             :  *   Synchronized instance is not supported and must be avoided.
      93                 :             :  *
      94                 :             :  * The intended usage is simple, non-reentrant critical sections:
      95                 :             :  * @code
      96                 :             :  * Synchronized<Foo> f;
      97                 :             :  * f.WithLock([](Foo& x) { x.do_something(); });
      98                 :             :  * @endcode
      99                 :             :  */
